His warning is concrete: strict vegans who don't supplement minerals correctly tend, within 5 years, to develop grey hair, receding gums, periodontal disease, arthritis, osteoporosis, anemia, hypertension, chronic fatigue, even cancer and liver cirrhosis — because an unsupplemented plant diet leaves them 51 to 57 of the body's essential minerals short (plants can't manufacture minerals).

WAL-CLM-IMMORT-000223.subject: chicken
WAL-CLM-IMMORT-000223.question: Does Wallach think chicken and other poultry belong in a healthy diet, or should we go vegan?
WAL-CLM-IMMORT-000223.answer_short: Wallach is firmly against going vegan and puts chicken squarely inside a healthy, long-life diet. His core claim: every long-lived population on earth eats animal foods — red meat (pork, beef, goat, lamb), poultry, fish, eggs and dairy — and no vegan, he says, has ever lived to 100 or raised a thriving colony of healthy kids on the diet. Unsupplemented strict vegans, he warns, tend to develop grey hair, receding gums, osteoporosis, anemia, arthritis and even cancer within 5 years, and he points to vegan crusader Linda McCartney, who died at 56 of breast cancer. So poultry isn't something to avoid — it's part of what he sees as a longevity diet, not a food to apologize for.

WAL-CLM-IMMORT-000224.subject: chicken
WAL-CLM-IMMORT-000224.question: Is fried chicken okay to eat?
WAL-CLM-IMMORT-000224.answer_short: Wallach lumps commercial fried chicken in with French fries, fried seafood, high-fructose corn syrup, soft drinks and white flour as things the world's longest-lived ('Blue Zone') peoples have no access to — the frying and processing is the problem, framing fried chicken as a food of ill health.

WAL-CLM-IMMORT-000225.subject: chicken
WAL-CLM-IMMORT-000225.question: How can I actually see that bone is made of both calcium and protein?
WAL-CLM-IMMORT-000225.answer_short: Wallach's kitchen demonstration: soak a chicken drumstick bone in a quart of vinegar for 2 weeks and the acid leaches out the calcium, leaving behind the rubbery protein matrix — showing bone is a protein framework mineralized with calcium, not solid rock.

WAL-CLM-IMMORT-000226.subject: chicken
WAL-CLM-IMMORT-000226.question: What can chickens teach us about human joint disease like carpal tunnel?
WAL-CLM-IMMORT-000226.answer_short: Wallach uses poultry as the model: arsenic plus the B-vitamin choline prevents 100% of perosis ('slipped tendon') in chickens, and the same arsenic deficiency in humans shows up as carpal tunnel syndrome, TMJ and other repetitive-motion joint diseases.

WAL-CLM-IMMORT-000227.subject: chicken
WAL-CLM-IMMORT-000227.question: How has chicken been viewed in traditional healing systems?
WAL-CLM-IMMORT-000227.answer_short: Relaying Taoist Chinese tradition, Wallach notes poultry (with vegetables and fish) is held to nourish the heart, lungs and kidneys under the five-element organ correspondences.

WAL-CLM-IMMORT-000228.subject: chicken
WAL-CLM-IMMORT-000228.question: What is a pollo-vegetarian?
WAL-CLM-IMMORT-000228.answer_short: Wallach defines a 'pollo-vegetarian' as really an omnivore who eats poultry (chicken) on top of grains, vegetables, fruit and nuts — part of his point that most self-described vegetarians actually eat animal foods.

WAL-CLM-IMMORT-000229.subject: pork
WAL-CLM-IMMORT-000229.question: Does Wallach think pork is healthy, or should it be avoided?
WAL-CLM-IMMORT-000229.answer_short: Wallach counts pork as a legitimate red meat — he points out that every long-lived people on earth eats it, so it is sound animal protein, not a food to shun.

WAL-CLM-IMMORT-000230.subject: pork
WAL-CLM-IMMORT-000230.question: Why does Wallach warn against ham, bacon, and sausage?
WAL-CLM-IMMORT-000230.answer_short: The nitrates and nitrites cured into ham, bacon, sausage and other processed pork act as goitrogens, interfering with normal thyroid metabolism and capable of producing thyroid disease.

WAL-CLM-IMMORT-000231.subject: pork
WAL-CLM-IMMORT-000231.question: Do any famously long-lived people eat pork?
WAL-CLM-IMMORT-000231.answer_short: Yes — and they may be the best example there is. Wallach points to the Okinawans, whom the World Health Organization ranked in 1996 as the longest-lived people in the entire industrialized world, and boiled pork is a staple of their roughly 1,500-calorie daily diet. He puts their life expectancy at 78 years for men and 86 for women, with a documented centenarian rate of 5 per 10,000 people — and, citing the 25-year Okinawa Centenarian Study, he credits their lifestyle and mineral-rich diet, not their genes, for that longevity. Their table alongside the pork includes chicken, eggs, dried minnows, miso and fish soup, tofu, sea and garden vegetables, kelp, garlic, purple sweet potatoes and bitter melon.

WAL-CLM-IMMORT-000232.subject: eggs
WAL-CLM-IMMORT-000232.question: Are eggs a good source of vitamin B12?
WAL-CLM-IMMORT-000232.answer_short: Wallach lists eggs among the rich dietary sources of vitamin B12, alongside liver, kidney, whole milk, cheese, and muscle meats, relevant because vegans risk B12 deficiency without it.

WAL-CLM-LETS-000080.subject: diabetes
WAL-CLM-LETS-000080.question: Can a normal blood test miss diabetes?
WAL-CLM-LETS-000080.answer_short: Yes — a single fasting blood-sugar reading misses most diabetes and hypoglycemia; Wallach says only a six-hour glucose tolerance test reveals them.

WAL-CLM-LETS-000083.subject: macrobiotics
WAL-CLM-LETS-000083.question: Why does the macrobiotic (brown-rice) diet work?
WAL-CLM-LETS-000083.answer_short: Wallach's take: its successes come mostly from accidentally cutting gluten - people with hidden celiac disease finally absorb minerals, vitamins and fats. The value is nutritional, not the yin/yang theory.

WAL-CLM-LETS-000084.subject: light_therapy
WAL-CLM-LETS-000084.question: What does ultraviolet (UV) light therapy treat?
WAL-CLM-LETS-000084.answer_short: Wallach says UV light boosts vitamin D and the immune system, and treats sore throats, vaginitis, ringworm, athlete's foot and eczema.

WAL-CLM-LETS-000085.subject: light_therapy
WAL-CLM-LETS-000085.question: How is infrared light therapy done?
WAL-CLM-LETS-000085.answer_short: A local immune boost - shine infrared (a heat lamp) on a trigger point through a 1 cm hole until it reddens, drawing in white cells to help chronic wounds, bedsores and arthritis.

WAL-CLM-LETS-000086.subject: light_therapy
WAL-CLM-LETS-000086.question: Is UV light therapy safe for the eyes?
WAL-CLM-LETS-000086.answer_short: Therapeutic UV is 'cool' (no heat) and helps skin diseases and arthritis while killing germs - but it can burn the eyes, so wear goggles or don't look at the lamp.

WAL-CLM-LETS-000087.subject: light_therapy
WAL-CLM-LETS-000087.question: How does UV therapy actually work?
WAL-CLM-LETS-000087.answer_short: Its rays span 500-3,100 Angstroms, peaking at 2,537 - the wavelength that gives UV its germicidal, skin-reddening and vitamin-D-making power; visible light is only ~5% of the output.

WAL-CLM-LETS-000088.subject: chiropractic
WAL-CLM-LETS-000088.question: What is chiropractic?
WAL-CLM-LETS-000088.answer_short: A drug-free, surgery-free physical medicine holding that many ills come from 'subluxations' (misaligned vertebrae) pressing on spinal nerves - the West's most accepted alternative therapy.

WAL-CLM-LETS-000089.subject: chiropractic
WAL-CLM-LETS-000089.question: Where does chiropractic come from?
WAL-CLM-LETS-000089.answer_short: Spinal manipulation is ancient (Egypt, China, Babylon); it reached the West in 1895 when D.D. Palmer reportedly cured a janitor's deafness, and chiropractors won a 1987 antitrust case against the AMA.

WAL-CLM-LETS-000090.subject: somatic_therapies
WAL-CLM-LETS-000090.question: What is osteopathy?
WAL-CLM-LETS-000090.answer_short: A manipulation-based healing art of body and spine, founded ~130 years ago by engineer Andrew Still after he lost all three children to orthodox medicine; today most D.O.s practice much like M.D.s.

WAL-CLM-LETS-000091.subject: somatic_therapies
WAL-CLM-LETS-000091.question: What is reflexology, and how is it meant to work?
WAL-CLM-LETS-000091.answer_short: An ancient Chinese and East Indian system: 'zones' on the soles and palms map to the internal organs, so 10-30 minutes of thumb compression on a point is meant to treat the organ it stands for.

WAL-CLM-LETS-000092.subject: somatic_therapies
WAL-CLM-LETS-000092.question: What is Rolfing (structural integration)?
WAL-CLM-LETS-000092.answer_short: A deep, uncomfortable connective-tissue massage devised by Ida Rolf to break down 'pathological' tissue and correct posture - said to leave patients half an inch to an inch taller.

WAL-CLM-LETS-000093.subject: aromatherapy
WAL-CLM-LETS-000093.question: What is aromatherapy?
WAL-CLM-LETS-000093.answer_short: Massage with plant essential oils (from roots, flowers, leaves, bark, resin); Wallach says they act as pesticides, fungicides and hormone-like agents and help scars, acne and stretch marks.

WAL-CLM-LETS-000094.subject: aromatherapy
WAL-CLM-LETS-000094.question: What are specific essential oils used for?
WAL-CLM-LETS-000094.answer_short: Wallach's list: Mexican yam for birth control, sarsaparilla for testosterone, peppermint for intestinal spasm, calamus to lower blood pressure, lemon as an expectorant, and hops/fennel for estrogens.

WAL-CLM-LETS-000095.subject: ayurveda
WAL-CLM-LETS-000095.question: What is Ayurveda, and how old is it?
WAL-CLM-LETS-000095.answer_short: Possibly the most ancient medical art - 'ayur' (life) + 'veda' (science), recorded ~1200 BC. 80-90% of Indians use it, and Wallach says the Greeks (even Pythagoras) learned medicine from the East Indians.

WAL-CLM-LETS-000096.subject: ayurveda
WAL-CLM-LETS-000096.question: How does Ayurveda explain health and disease?
WAL-CLM-LETS-000096.answer_short: The body is seven tissues (Dhatus) kept in balance by food, so 'wrong food' causes disease; it works with the energies Pitta, Kapha and Vaya and five elements, treating imbalances rather than diagnoses.

WAL-CLM-LETS-000097.subject: homeopathy
WAL-CLM-LETS-000097.question: What are Schuessler cell salts (Biochemics)?
WAL-CLM-LETS-000097.answer_short: A 19th-century system from Dr. Wilhelm Schuessler, who analyzed the ash of cremated bodies and found twelve mineral 'salts' he called essential to health; given in homeopathic (highly diluted) doses. Later workers added ~30 trace elements.

WAL-CLM-LETS-000098.subject: homeopathy
WAL-CLM-LETS-000098.question: What are Bach flower remedies?
WAL-CLM-LETS-000098.answer_short: Homeopathic-style flower preparations from bacteriologist Edward Bach (1880-1936), who first collected sun-warmed flower dew; aimed at emotional imbalance rather than physical disease, taken as four drops four times a day.

WAL-CLM-LETS-000099.subject: color_therapy
WAL-CLM-LETS-000099.question: What is color therapy?
WAL-CLM-LETS-000099.answer_short: Using colored lights or panels for a healing effect — recorded in ancient Egypt and used in Ayurvedic and Chinese medicine; Wallach frames it as a form of light therapy.

WAL-CLM-LETS-000100.subject: color_therapy
WAL-CLM-LETS-000100.question: What does each color treat in color therapy?
WAL-CLM-LETS-000100.answer_short: Wallach's color map: blue for blood pressure, fever, cuts and burns; red for low blood pressure; orange for stones; yellow for diabetes; green for ulcers, colds and breast cancer.

WAL-CLM-LETS-000101.subject: color_therapy
WAL-CLM-LETS-000101.question: How is color therapy actually done?
WAL-CLM-LETS-000101.answer_short: Six techniques — the Kilner diagnostic screen, reading tissue colors, sun-charged salt bags, colored foods, 'rainbow' sun-charged water, and meditative color breathing.

WAL-CLM-LETS-000102.subject: faith_healing
WAL-CLM-LETS-000102.question: What is faith healing (laying-on-of-hands)?
WAL-CLM-LETS-000102.answer_short: Using a person to mediate healing through belief - recorded in ancient China and Egypt and in Christianity today. Wallach notes 20-60% of patients improve on placebo when positive thought is induced.

WAL-CLM-LETS-000103.subject: faith_healing
WAL-CLM-LETS-000103.question: Who are the Christian Scientists, and what is 'therapeutic touch'?
WAL-CLM-LETS-000103.answer_short: A Christian sect founded in 1879 by Mary Baker Eddy that holds 'healing is proof of God's love'; Wallach says they outlive other Westerners (and get lower insurance rates). Its modern nursing form is 'therapeutic touch.'

WAL-CLM-LETS-000104.subject: herbal_medicine
WAL-CLM-LETS-000104.question: What is herbal medicine?
WAL-CLM-LETS-000104.answer_short: An ancient system using plants to prevent and cure disease - the root of Chinese, Ayurvedic, American Indian and naturopathic medicine, traced back to Chinese pharmacopeias around 3000 BC.

WAL-CLM-LETS-000105.subject: herbal_medicine
WAL-CLM-LETS-000105.question: Do real drugs come from herbs?
WAL-CLM-LETS-000105.answer_short: Yes - Wallach notes over 30% of orthodox pharmaceuticals derive from plants (digitalis from foxglove, the cancer drug vincristine from periwinkle), and praises herbs' relative safety and millennia of use.

WAL-CLM-LETS-000106.subject: hydrotherapy
WAL-CLM-LETS-000106.question: What is hydrotherapy?
WAL-CLM-LETS-000106.answer_short: Healing with water - practiced since Roman times across all medicine, from sitz baths for hemorrhoids to whirlpools for injuries and mineral baths for arthritis; insurance often covers it if prescribed.

WAL-CLM-LETS-000107.subject: hydrotherapy
WAL-CLM-LETS-000107.question: What are the different kinds of hydrotherapy?
WAL-CLM-LETS-000107.answer_short: Cold baths cut swelling; hot baths ease soreness; mineral baths help arthritis; steam baths detox heavy metals; sitz baths for hemorrhoids; epsom for edema; water fasts and colonics for detox.

WAL-CLM-LETS-000108.subject: negative_ion_therapy
WAL-CLM-LETS-000108.question: What is negative ion therapy?
WAL-CLM-LETS-000108.answer_short: Using negatively charged air particles to prevent and treat disease - abundant in forests and at the beach (300-1,000 per cubic meter) but low in AC'd rooms; too many POSITIVE ions bring anxiety and depression.

WAL-CLM-LETS-000109.subject: negative_ion_therapy
WAL-CLM-LETS-000109.question: What does negative ion therapy do?
WAL-CLM-LETS-000109.answer_short: Six effects - it lowers heart rate/BP, deepens breathing, speeds respiratory cilia, boosts glands and steadies brain rhythm - and Wallach says it especially helps asthma, allergies and cystic fibrosis.

WAL-CLM-LETS-000110.subject: urine_therapy
WAL-CLM-LETS-000110.question: What is urine therapy?
WAL-CLM-LETS-000110.answer_short: Injecting a patient's own urine back into them to boost immunity - the same idea as an allergist's shots; Wallach says MD allergists used it for 50 years until prepared allergens became profitable.

WAL-CLM-LETS-000111.subject: urine_therapy
WAL-CLM-LETS-000111.question: How is urine therapy performed?
WAL-CLM-LETS-000111.answer_short: Urine is centrifuged and filtered to remove cells and bacteria, then 5-10 mL is injected under the skin (procaine stops any sting); Wallach cites use for allergies, asthma, migraine and arthritis.

WAL-CLM-LETS-000112.subject: homeopathy
WAL-CLM-LETS-000112.question: What is homeopathy?
WAL-CLM-LETS-000112.answer_short: A system on two principles: 'like cures like' (a substance that causes symptoms in the healthy can cure a disease with those symptoms) and 'minimum dose' - using extremely diluted preparations.

WAL-CLM-LETS-000113.subject: homeopathy
WAL-CLM-LETS-000113.question: Who founded homeopathy, and does the dilution really work?
WAL-CLM-LETS-000113.answer_short: Samuel Hahnemann, who found Cinchona bark gave healthy people malaria-like symptoms; oddly, more dilute often meant a stronger effect - though past about 12C not one molecule of the original remains.

WAL-CLM-LETS-000114.subject: naturopathy
WAL-CLM-LETS-000114.question: What is naturopathy?
WAL-CLM-LETS-000114.answer_short: A whole system of natural medicine (N.D.) built on 'FIRST DO NO HARM' and the body's own healing power - covering herbs, hydrotherapy, homeopathy, nutrition and natural childbirth, but not major surgery or most drugs.

WAL-CLM-LETS-000115.subject: macrobiotics
WAL-CLM-LETS-000115.question: Where did macrobiotics come from?
WAL-CLM-LETS-000115.answer_short: George Ohsawa created it in 1946 Japan, using it to heal his own tuberculosis, then opened a healing center and toured the world teaching a philosophy of health through eating.

WAL-CLM-LETS-000116.subject: macrobiotics
WAL-CLM-LETS-000116.question: What is the macrobiotic diet?
WAL-CLM-LETS-000116.answer_short: An eating system built on balancing 'yin' (fruit, drinks, sweet) and 'yang' (meat, grains, dense) foods; reported to help food allergies, diabetes and - when wheat is dropped - grain sensitivity.

WAL-CLM-LETS-000117.subject: vitamins
WAL-CLM-LETS-000117.question: What is megavitamin (orthomolecular) therapy?
WAL-CLM-LETS-000117.answer_short: Using vitamins at very high 'pharmacologic' doses - the 1968 'megavitamin theory' that Linus Pauling named 'orthomolecular medicine' and Abram Hoffer extended to psychiatry, reportedly for colds, depression and schizophrenia, though orthodoxy never endorsed it.

WAL-CLM-LETS-000194.subject: urine_therapy
WAL-CLM-LETS-000194.question: How do autoimmune urine and blood therapies work?
WAL-CLM-LETS-000194.answer_short: They rev the body's defenses against foreign substances - including cancer proteins - much the way allergy shots build tolerance to pollen.

WAL-CLM-LETS-000209.subject: gluten
WAL-CLM-LETS-000209.question: What does celiac disease do to absorption, and can the gut heal?
WAL-CLM-LETS-000209.answer_short: Wheat gluten can destroy up to 70% of the intestine's absorptive surface (90% by age 45–50). Wallach says removing the offending grain lets the gut repair over about 90 days.

WAL-CLM-LETS-000232.subject: pregnancy_birth
WAL-CLM-LETS-000232.question: Why were midwives who knew contraception called witches?
WAL-CLM-LETS-000232.answer_short: Wallach notes midwives who knew contraception herbs were once branded 'witches' and burned; he ranks birth control (abstinence, barriers, hormones - least desirable, IUDs, surgery) and bluntly calls sex outside marriage 'Russian roulette.'

WAL-CLM-LETS-000263.subject: sexual_health
WAL-CLM-LETS-000263.question: How does Wallach approach premature ejaculation?
WAL-CLM-LETS-000263.answer_short: He calls it normal and curable, with physical causes (high expectation, infrequent sex, friction) not guilt; his fix is comfort with each other's bodies, frequent sex, and good lubrication, with ginseng and Zumbani as tonics.

WAL-CLM-LETS-000312.subject: vaccines
WAL-CLM-LETS-000312.question: What is Wallach's stance on vaccine mandates?
WAL-CLM-LETS-000312.answer_short: He calls immunization 'the greatest interface between government and freedom of choice,' opposes compulsory school mandates, defends the religious exemption, and says some experts blame certain vaccine programs for catastrophic diseases.

WAL-CLM-LETS-000347.subject: longevity
WAL-CLM-LETS-000347.question: How long can humans live?
WAL-CLM-LETS-000347.answer_short: Wallach says 120-130 years, vs the ~72-78 of actuary tables. He credits the Hunza's ~100-year average to plant-derived colloidal minerals, and says filters, digestive aids and the baseline program add ~20 years.

WAL-CLM-LETS-000362.subject: be_your_own_doctor
WAL-CLM-LETS-000362.question: What is 'metabolic therapy'?
WAL-CLM-LETS-000362.answer_short: Wallach's umbrella term for curing disease by fixing whole-body metabolism - through nutrition, herbs, homeopathy, acupuncture, manipulation and hydrotherapy.

WAL-CLM-LETS-000370.subject: home_remedies
WAL-CLM-LETS-000370.question: How can you repel mosquitoes naturally?
WAL-CLM-LETS-000370.answer_short: Screen doors and 'zapper' lights set 15-25 yards from the house draw mosquitoes off; Wallach adds pennyroyal oil on the skin and vitamin B1 at 500 mg/day as natural repellents - handy since mosquitoes carry malaria and encephalitis.

WAL-CLM-LETS-000467.subject: pregnancy_birth
WAL-CLM-LETS-000467.question: Is a hospital birth necessary?
WAL-CLM-LETS-000467.answer_short: Wallach says pregnancy is normal, not a disease, and home birth is the safest, cheapest option - he delivered ~200 babies at home with one c-section, and blames the 35% hospital c-section rate on economics.

WAL-CLM-LETS-000468.subject: pregnancy_birth
WAL-CLM-LETS-000468.question: What prenatal care can a woman do herself?
WAL-CLM-LETS-000468.answer_short: A lot: self breast and pelvic exams, cycle tracking, home pregnancy tests, OTC prenatal vitamins, own blood-pressure and urine tests - and, barring a few specific risks, she can give birth at home.

WAL-CLM-LETS-000469.subject: pregnancy_birth
WAL-CLM-LETS-000469.question: What birth control can you buy without a prescription?
WAL-CLM-LETS-000469.answer_short: Condoms, spermicidal creams, jellies, foams and sponges - all over the counter. Wallach considers these barrier methods much safer than IUDs (the Dalkon Shield) and the pill (clots, deaths, sterility).

WAL-CLM-LETS-000470.subject: pregnancy_birth
WAL-CLM-LETS-000470.question: What causes most birth defects?
WAL-CLM-LETS-000470.answer_short: Wallach's 'pet peeve': 98% come from nutritional deficiencies, not radiation. Teens have more than women over 40 - and lab animals get defect-free diets, so why feed a rat better than a pregnant woman?

WAL-CLM-LETS-000471.subject: cystic_fibrosis
WAL-CLM-LETS-000471.question: Is cystic fibrosis really genetic?
WAL-CLM-LETS-000471.answer_short: Wallach's signature thesis: no - it's a selenium and essential-fatty-acid deficiency from the mother's malabsorption. He cites 1972 Cornell chicks cured in 21 days by selenium, and 450 patients treated since 1978.

WAL-CLM-LETS-000472.subject: pregnancy_birth
WAL-CLM-LETS-000472.question: Is infertility a nutrition problem?
WAL-CLM-LETS-000472.answer_short: Wallach says mostly yes - as a breeder feeds a mare 120 days before mating, he's reversed hundreds of cases by nourishing both partners; one 'infertile' doctor had vitamin A at 10% of normal (malabsorption).

WAL-CLM-LETS-000473.subject: be_your_own_doctor
WAL-CLM-LETS-000473.question: How should you choose a medical specialist?
WAL-CLM-LETS-000473.answer_short: Only when truly needed - then get three-plus opinions from different fields, ask to speak with ten past patients, and start conservative; the more 'exotic' the specialist, the higher the risk.

WAL-CLM-LETS-000474.subject: be_your_own_doctor
WAL-CLM-LETS-000474.question: How impaired are conventional doctors?
WAL-CLM-LETS-000474.answer_short: Wallach cites alarming numbers - tens of thousands of physician alcoholics, heavy drug use among doctors and students, and the U.S. losing 'seven medical-school classes' a year to addiction and suicide.

WAL-CLM-LETS-000475.subject: be_your_own_doctor
WAL-CLM-LETS-000475.question: What does Wallach mean by 'be your own doctor'?
WAL-CLM-LETS-000475.answer_short: Become your own primary care provider - you're unlikely to harm yourself. Try conservative and alternative care before orthodox medicine, and 'separate medicine and state.'

WAL-CLM-LETS-000476.subject: be_your_own_doctor
WAL-CLM-LETS-000476.question: What's the best health insurance?
WAL-CLM-LETS-000476.answer_short: Not getting sick. Prevention - a baseline supplement program and daily self-care - is cheaper and easier than illness; Wallach calls it the best buy for your health dollars.

WAL-CLM-LETS-000477.subject: hospital_dangers
WAL-CLM-LETS-000477.question: How dangerous are hospitals?
WAL-CLM-LETS-000477.answer_short: Wallach's tally: 970 of 1,000 hospitals billed wrong (always in their favor), up to half of new equipment defective on arrival, and 100,000+ deaths a year from hospital-caught infections.

WAL-CLM-LETS-000478.subject: hospital_dangers
WAL-CLM-LETS-000478.question: What should you do if you're hospitalized?
WAL-CLM-LETS-000478.answer_short: Have a family member stay to check every shot, pill and procedure before it's given, confirm your IV lines, and use family blood if needed - just as orthodox doctors monitor their own families.

WAL-CLM-LETS-000479.subject: hospital_dangers
WAL-CLM-LETS-000479.question: What is the 'medical industrial Bermuda Triangle'?
WAL-CLM-LETS-000479.answer_short: Wallach's name for the FDA, AMA and drug companies - costing Americans more than national defense while the U.S. ranks 17th in longevity and 32nd in birth defects. He calls to 'separate Medicine and State.'

WAL-CLM-LETS-000480.subject: pregnancy_birth
WAL-CLM-LETS-000480.question: Which agency said women should supplement before pregnancy?
WAL-CLM-LETS-000480.answer_short: The CDC, in 1992 - not the FDA. Wallach credits the CDC's independence from company revenue, and notes it independently echoed his own preconception-supplementation thesis.

WAL-CLM-LETS-000481.subject: be_your_own_doctor
WAL-CLM-LETS-000481.question: How do you take charge of your home environment?
WAL-CLM-LETS-000481.answer_short: Grow some food and treat your home water and air - Wallach says 3,000+ mostly-carcinogenic chemicals slip through city water (clear isn't safe); a bone-charcoal filter removes them.

WAL-CLM-LETS-000482.subject: phytates
WAL-CLM-LETS-000482.question: Can phytates block even supplemented calcium?
WAL-CLM-LETS-000482.answer_short: Yes — Wallach calls phytates a natural chelating substance in plants that can make even supplemented calcium unavailable.

WAL-CLM-LETS-000483.subject: carbonated_beverages
WAL-CLM-LETS-000483.question: Are carbonated soft drinks bad for you, even diet soda?
WAL-CLM-LETS-000483.answer_short: Cut sugar and caffeine, and drop soft drinks; even diet sodas are full of phosphates that drive osteoporosis.

WAL-CLM-LETS-000484.subject: beef
WAL-CLM-LETS-000484.question: Is there any condition where Wallach says to avoid beef entirely?
WAL-CLM-LETS-000484.answer_short: Yes. For lupus (SLE), Wallach explicitly says to avoid beef, along with dairy and alfalfa, as part of treatment.

WAL-CLM-LETS-000485.subject: beef
WAL-CLM-LETS-000485.question: Is it dangerous to eat rare or undercooked beef?
WAL-CLM-LETS-000485.answer_short: Wallach warns that rare beef can transmit toxoplasmosis, especially dangerous for pregnant women because it can cause fetal birth defects such as brain damage, blindness and mental retardation.

WAL-CLM-LETS-000486.subject: pork
WAL-CLM-LETS-000486.question: Can eating pork trigger a gallbladder attack?
WAL-CLM-LETS-000486.answer_short: Yes. Wallach says pork ranks close behind eggs and onions as a food that precipitates gallbladder attacks.

WAL-CLM-LETS-000487.subject: pork
WAL-CLM-LETS-000487.question: Can you get parasites or tapeworms from pork?
WAL-CLM-LETS-000487.answer_short: Yes. Wallach warns that raw pork is one of the foods that transmits tapeworm; the encysted larvae hatch in the gut and latch onto the intestinal wall.

WAL-CLM-LETS-000488.subject: fish
WAL-CLM-LETS-000488.question: How does fish oil help cholesterol / heart health?
WAL-CLM-LETS-000488.answer_short: The EPA in fish oil (and flax oil) raises protective HDL cholesterol — the fraction that ferries cholesterol to the liver for disposal — while refined sugar drives HDL down to dangerous levels.

WAL-CLM-RARE-000112.subject: rare_earth_elements
WAL-CLM-RARE-000112.question: Does cerium have a medical use?
WAL-CLM-RARE-000112.answer_short: Yes -- cerium (a rare earth that accumulates in bone) is used as cerium nitrate, a topical disinfectant for severe burn victims.

WAL-CLM-RARE-000276.subject: drug_safety_elderly
WAL-CLM-RARE-000276.question: Which tranquilizers and sleeping pills are risky for older adults?
WAL-CLM-RARE-000276.answer_short: Wallach flags Valium (diazepam), Librium (chlordiazepoxide) and Dalmane (flurazepam) as too long-acting or addictive -- they cause drowsiness, confusion and falls in the elderly. His fix: address the underlying need with minerals (calcium, magnesium, lithium, chromium, vanadium) and cut sugar and caffeine.

WAL-CLM-RARE-000277.subject: drug_safety_elderly
WAL-CLM-RARE-000277.question: What other tranquilizers and sleeping pills should older adults avoid?
WAL-CLM-RARE-000277.answer_short: The second half of Wallach's list: Miltown (meprobamate), Nembutal (pentobarbital) and Seconal (secobarbital) -- all addictive, long-acting and fall-prone. Same mineral replacement: calcium, magnesium, lithium, chromium and vanadium.

WAL-CLM-RARE-000284.subject: drug_safety_elderly
WAL-CLM-RARE-000284.question: Which muscle relaxants are risky for older adults?
WAL-CLM-RARE-000284.answer_short: Wallach flags Flexeril (cyclobenzaprine), Norflex (orphenadrine), Robaxin (methocarbamol) and Soma (carisoprodol) -- they cause dizziness, drowsiness, fainting and falls. His mineral replacement: calcium, magnesium, boron and lithium.

WAL-CLM-RARE-000312.subject: salt
WAL-CLM-RARE-000312.question: Does Wallach think salt is bad for you?
WAL-CLM-RARE-000312.answer_short: Wallach calls salt a craved necessity and the universal food condiment; a saltless bread-and-water diet was once a dreaded Dutch punishment.

WAL-CLM-RARE-000313.subject: sugar
WAL-CLM-RARE-000313.question: Why do I crave sugar and soft drinks?
WAL-CLM-RARE-000313.answer_short: Craving soft drinks and sweets is a sign of chromium and vanadium deficiency, not real hunger.

WAL-CLM-RARE-000314.subject: butter
WAL-CLM-RARE-000314.question: What should I cook with instead of margarine or vegetable oil?
WAL-CLM-RARE-000314.answer_short: In his See-Food Diet free-radical-elimination list, Wallach gives a flat cooking directive: no margarine — cook with butter, ghee, mutton fat, or water instead. Butter is on his approved-fats shortlist for the kitchen.

WAL-CLM-RARE-000315.subject: chicken
WAL-CLM-RARE-000315.question: Is chicken soup actually useful when you're sick with the flu?
WAL-CLM-RARE-000315.answer_short: Yes. Wallach holds up chicken soup — with the herbs echinacea and goldenseal plus a dose of bismuth — as the safe, effective nutritional way to handle the flu (which he frames as dehydration and diarrhea). His cautionary contrast is George Washington, who had influenza but was killed by his doctors, not the illness: in a little over 12 hours they drained him of 80 to 90 ounces of blood (6 pints), dosed him with calomel (mercury) and emetic tartar (antimony), and blistered his skin and throat, until Washington himself begged to be allowed to die in peace. The lesson Wallach draws is blunt — a grandmother's bowl of chicken soup would have served the 'Father of our Country' better than the best physicians of his day.

WAL-CLM-RARE-000316.subject: chicken
WAL-CLM-RARE-000316.question: What nutrients does chicken provide — is it a source of dietary fat?
WAL-CLM-RARE-000316.answer_short: Wallach lists chicken among the primary food sources of dietary fats/lipids (with pork, fish, beef and lamb), the animal fats that supply energy alongside plant oils, nuts and dairy.

WAL-CLM-RARE-000317.subject: eggs
WAL-CLM-RARE-000317.question: Can eating eggs help with menopause symptoms?
WAL-CLM-RARE-000317.answer_short: Because cholesterol is the raw material the body uses to make estrogen, Wallach says eating 2 eggs every morning supplies that raw material and lets a woman slip through menopause almost symptom-free.

WAL-CLM-RARE-000318.subject: fish
WAL-CLM-RARE-000318.question: Is canned tuna worse than fresh tuna?
WAL-CLM-RARE-000318.answer_short: Canned tuna carries nearly double the lead of fresh tuna, because the sealant used on can seams leaches lead into the food.
